metadata.description: Absolute hypsometric tint of the GEM-15 15 m DSM, with an Igor hillshade laid over it. Colour is keyed to true elevation in meters above the EGM96 geoid, from the Dead Sea shore (-430 m) to the high Himalaya, so the same color means the same height anywhere on Earth. Because this is a DSM, buildings, canopy and other surface cover are part of the terrain: city blocks read as plateaus and forest edges as cliffs. GEM-15 encodes NaN and ocean alike as 0 m, so the 0 m stop is painted as water and doubles as the no-data tone; tiles inside the excluded countries therefore read as sea level rather than as a gap. Coverage runs 84N to 61S and excludes Russia, China, Mongolia and Greenland.
metadata.portolan:ramp: Stops in meters (EGM96): -430 #0f3d2e, -5 #1d5c42, 0 #5d7f93 (water / no-data), 1 #2d6a3f, 100 #4e8c4a, 300 #7aa85a, 600 #a8c06a, 900 #cfcf7d, 1200 #e2cf8c, 1600 #d8b074, 2000 #c0905c, 2400 #a4744a, 2800 #8a5c3e, 3200 #745038, 3600 #6d5b50, 4200 #8a7d74, 4800 #a99d95, 5400 #c9c0ba, 6000 #e6e2df, 6800 #ffffff, 8849 #ffffff. The deliberate 0 m to 1 m step puts a hard coastline between the water tone and the lowland greens.
metadata.portolan:palette-note: Google's own GEM-15 visualization (the Earth Engine example script) uses an 11-color palette applied cyclically, elevation modulo 100 m. That is a relief-reading device, not an elevation scale: it shows fine vertical structure beautifully but the same color recurs at 40 m, 140 m and 240 m. It is modular, so it cannot express absolute height and is unsuited to an absolute ramp. The cyclic palette is reproduced in this collection's overview COG instead; this style uses a conventional absolute hypsometric ramp so that color carries height.
metadata.portolan:caveats: Elevations are meters above the EGM96 geoid, not ellipsoidal heights and not EGM2008; apply a geoid correction before combining with other DEMs for altimetry. Surface model (DSM), not bare earth. India is intentionally offset upstream.
